key_insight: HalluGuard introduces a unified way to detect and quantify two distinct sources of LLM hallucinations—data-driven and reasoning-driven—so that failures can be identified and addressed systematically. It moves beyond task-specific heuristics by providing a general, risk-based framework for measuring hallucination likelihood.
problem_solved: Existing hallucination detectors focus on either source (bad or missing evidence vs. faulty internal reasoning) and rely on task-specific rules, limiting generalization; this paper provides a single, task-agnostic approach to distinguish, quantify, and detect both types of hallucinations.
method: Define a clear taxonomy and risk metric that separates data-driven hallucinations (unsupported by external evidence) from reasoning-driven hallucinations (internal inference errors).

Compute hallucination risk by cross-checking model outputs against retrieved or known evidence for data risk and by assessing internal reasoning consistency (e.g., chain-of-thought checks, contradiction detection) for reasoning risk.
Combine these signals into a unified HalluGuard detector and benchmark that is model- and task-agnostic, enabling calibrated alerts and prioritized mitigation strategies.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical, generalizable tool to detect and prioritize hallucination types, improving trust and targeted mitigation in high-stakes applications (healthcare, law, science). This enables better monitoring, debugging, and intervention selection across diverse tasks and models.

paper_title: HalluGuard: Demystifying Data-Driven and Reasoning-Driven Hallucinations in LLMs
paper_authors: Xinyue Zeng, Junhong Lin, Yujun Yan, Feng Guo, Liang Shi
